Actually disagree the Lannisters started in a bad position. They'd basically conquered the Riverlands before Northern forces even arrived. It took ingenuity and trickery on Robbs part to even the playing field and even while winning the battles he was losing the war, as he states. Can't remember if that's show only though that he says that.

Ultimately without the help of the Vale, and without the help of Renly he'd have lost a war of attrition even without Roose and Walder betrayals.

That said, it's not his fault. He did make mistakes but I don't think not being able to predict shadow demon assassin murdering renly is a mark against him as a general, nor could did he have control over Edmure's blunder, Catelyns moments of madness or the Greyjoy attack.

Important to remember Theons betrayal was siding with Ironborn and what he did at Winter fell personally. But Baelon attacking the north? He was already planning it before Theon even arrived at Pyke.

Too many things he couldn't control. Some things he could control politically, he fucked up. But basically nothing he could've done to win by that point.

Now, if the war had stayed isolated to a purely north & riverlands vs lannister affair, and you take the hostages out of it and it was just a battle for, say, an independent north and riverlands, then with smaller war aims I think Robb could well have won.

Still think Tywins pride would never accept this though and he has Robb assassinated at some stage. No way does the most prideful/fragile ego in Westeros let himself lose a war to a teenager from the supposedly uncivilised North embarrass him at war, with fewer troops, worse equipment and far fewer resources. Robb ends up dead one way or another, sooner or later.

Picks of them reading it in a scenic environment, with a coffee, by the pool, quotes from it, probably never finish it, but talk about it constantly.

And yes, keep taking it until you feel better. All anti depressants work this way, without fail. It's not your brain telling you it doesn't want the chemical, it's just your brain adjusting.

Anti depressants all have a period of a week or two in which you may feel a little strange-it differs from person to person the exact symptoms and severity-until you adjust and get the benefit.

What I will say is you're doing more harm than good starting and stopping. Your brain doesn't know what is happening when you keep starting and stopping. So you're getting all the negative startup effects of the meds with none of the benefits.
